name: John Legge
description: A royal sergeant-at-arms blamed by contemporaries for devising the intrusive method used by the 1381 poll tax commissioners to physically inspect households for unregistered (and therefore untaxed) young women. Taken from the Tower on 14 June 1381 along with Sudbury and Hales and beheaded on Tower Hill.
narrative_function: Ties the Tower killings directly back to the poll tax's most personally intrusive enforcement method.
